incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: high memory pressure / OOMs on prod-gpu-pool-3 (detected 3175550000)
oncall-jen: Acked. I'm joining now — can someone post quick customer impact and top logs?
support-lucas: Seeing ~3 customer errors/min for completions in us-west, a handful of 500s. CS reports a widget failing for two customers. Not widespread but repeatable starting ~10:03
sre-miguel: Captured events from node-gpu-12: repeated CUDA OOM in runtime process, fragmentation + pagewalk spikes. Uploading logs: gs://redwood-incidents/3175550123/node-gpu-12/logs.tar.gz
runtime-ryan: Dumped GPU stats (snapshot at 10:05):
- total_mem: 48 GiB
- used_by_model: 39.2 GiB
- kv_cache_alloc: 5.6 GiB
- free_fragments: 1.4 GiB (highly fragmented)
- pagewalks/sec: 8200
- allocator_retries: 42

runtime-ryan: Quick ps output: processes shows many long-lived inference procs holding pinned pages; batch_size distribution shifted up after a deploy at 09:58
ml-anya: Note: we shipped model v3.7.1 at 09:55 which increased max_tokens default and changed request batching hints. Could be correlated.
oncall-jen: Hypothesis A: model change increased average sequence length -> KV cache growth -> fragmentation + OOM on hot nodes
oncall-jen: Hypothesis B: a customer sent a few very large-batch requests that triggered runaway allocator churn
sre-miguel: Evidence for A: kv_cache_alloc spike around 09:57 in prometheus. Link: https://prom.redwood/graph?g=kv_alloc&from=09:50&to=10:10
sre-miguel: Evidence for B: audit log shows two requests with batch_size=64 and seq_len~6k to the generation endpoint at 09:56 from key:cust-42
runtime-ryan: Repro CLI we used locally:
```
rbctl trace --node node-gpu-12 --since 09:50 --filter "alloc fail|OOM|pagewalk"
``` 
runtime-ryan: Immediate mitigation applied: lowered per-worker max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 via runtime flag, and enabled soft-eviction of KV entries older than 2h on node-gpu-12
oncall-jen: Observed effect: pagewalks/sec down to ~1200 after the change, allocator_retries dropped to 3
support-lucas: Customer errors dropped to near zero after mitigations. CS notified affected customers and applied small workaround on their side.
ml-anya: Longer term: we should tune default batching hints for v3.7.x and add a model-specific kv_cache cap or adaptive eviction policy
eng-prod-kate: Suggest a rolling rollback of v3.7.1 to v3.6.9 in prod as a safety net while we validate kv cache controls
sre-miguel: Timeline so far:
- 09:55 deploy v3.7.1
- 09:56 first large batch requests observed
- 09:57 kv_cache alloc spike
- 09:58 allocator errors begin
- 10:03 paging surge + OOMs
- 10:08 mitigation: reduce max_batch_size
- 10:18 soft-eviction enabled
- 10:35 metrics stable, low customer impact

runtime-ryan: Log excerpts (sanitized):
[10:03:12] runtime ERR: failed to allocate 128MB -> CUDA_OOM
[10:03:12] runtime WARN: fragmentation: free_chunks=[64MB,32MB,16MB,...], requested 128MB
[10:03:13] runtime INFO: kvcache size 5.6GB entries=129k
